record.paper_title: Subsums of Null Sequences: A Survey and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Infinite sums of middle-α Cantor sets
record.original_question: Let α_i and λ_i be null sequences with α_i → 0 and λ_i → 0, and for each i let K_i be the middle-α_i Cantor set whose first construction interval is [0, λ_i]. If S is the sumset formed from these K_i and R_z denotes the corresponding tail set, under what conditions on R_z and on the parameters α_i is S a Cantor set, and what kind of Cantor set can occur?

evidence.quote:
We pose the following open questions when considering S:
1. Under what conditions of Rz and αi for i ∈ N will this set be a Cantor
set? What type of Cantor set will it be?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each $i \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\alpha_i \in (0,1)$ and $\lambda_i > 0$ with $\alpha_i \to 0$ and $\lambda_i \to 0$. Define the middle-$\alpha_i$ Cantor set $K_i \subset [0, \lambda_i]$ as follows: start with the interval $[0, \lambda_i]$, remove the open middle subinterval of relative length $\alpha_i$, then iterate this middle-removal procedure on each remaining closed interval, and let $K_i$ be the intersection of all stages. Assume the sequence of diameters $\lambda_i$ is summable, and define the (infinite) sumset
$$S = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} x_i : x_i \in K_i \text{ for all } i \Bigr\} \subset \mathbb{R},$$
together with the tail sets
$$R_z = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=z+1}^{\infty} x_i : x_i \in K_i \text{ for } i > z \Bigr\}, \qquad z \in \mathbb{N}.$$
Recall that a Cantor set is a nonempty compact, perfect, totally disconnected subset of $\mathbb{R}$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters $\{\alpha_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ and on the tail sets $R_z$ under which $S$ is a Cantor set, and characterize which kinds of Cantor sets (e.g. self-similar, central, of prescribed Hausdorff dimension, etc.) can arise as $S$.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on subsum sets of null sequences (Guthrie–Nymann, Nitecki, and others) classifies such sets as finite unions of intervals, Cantor sets, or Cantorvals, but explicit necessary-and-sufficient conditions for infinite sumsets of middle-α Cantor sets with α_i → 0 to be Cantor sets, together with a classification of which Cantor sets occur, have not been located in the search results, and the question is posed as open in the survey on subsums of null sequences.

status_evidence.title: Cantorvals and Subsum Sets of Null Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: The subsum set of an absolutely summable sequence is a finite union of compact intervals, a Cantor set, or a symmetric Cantorval.
status_evidence.claim: The trichotomy classification is known but explicit conditions for the Cantor-set case in infinite sumsets of middle-α Cantor sets with vanishing parameters are not established.

status_evidence.title: Conditions for the Difference Set of a Central Cantor Set to be a Cantorval
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies conditions on central Cantor sets and their sumsets/difference sets to be Cantor sets or Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on related conditions, indicating the question is not closed.
